label: Nuxt 4
streaming: buffered (Nitro node-server renders the Vue app with renderToString and sends one body with Content-Length)
notes: Start: node .output/server/index.mjs (Nitro node-server preset, the documented Node deployment). It honours PORT and HOST (binds 127.0.0.1).

Compression: none. Nitro does not compress dynamic responses even when the client sends Accept-Encoding: gzip, br (compressPublicAssets is off by default and only affects pre-compressed static assets).

Per request on /items: Nitro router -> Vue SSR of the page; useFetch("/api/items") during SSR is served in-process by Nitro (local fetch to the server route, no socket), listItems() once, formatPrice on the server; the result is serialised into the Nuxt payload (devalue) inlined in the HTML. Response has x-powered-by: Nuxt, no cache headers.
Data module lives in server/lib/data.ts and is imported only by server/api routes, so it is never in the client bundle (checked: no seeded strings in .output/public/_nuxt).

Form: Nuxt has no form-action primitive; per the data-fetching docs, event-based POSTs use $fetch to a Nitro server route (server/api/items/index.post.ts, readFormData + validateName). Invalid -> createError 400 whose message the page shows in #form-error; valid -> addItem, returns {id}, page calls navigateTo(`/items/${id}`).
Without JS the <form method="post" action="/api/items"> still adds the item but the browser shows the JSON response (no redirect, no error page); Nuxt has no documented no-JS form path.

/items/:id: useFetch(`/api/items/${id}`); the route throws createError 404 for an unknown id, the page throws createError({ status: 404 }) when data is empty (error-handling docs example) -> HTTP 404.
NuxtLink default prefetch: visible links prefetch the target page component chunk on idle (the 100 item links share one route chunk).
Telemetry: telemetry: false in nuxt.config; the harness also sets NUXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1. devtools: { enabled: true } is the starter-template default and is dev-only.
